Backend: 7/7 tests pass in new test_jump_broadcast.py (fresh player _jump_start_ms=0, to_state() sin-arc for humans mid-jump, snap-back+reset after 650ms, bots unaffected, static asserts for MATCHED_USERS.pop line and jump WS handler). Also confirmed sockRef.send({type:'jump'}) fires successfully (jumpSent:true) after simulated space bind through WS.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 24 fixed two coupled bugs: (1) leave-loop — handleExit() now calls queueCtx.cancelRanked()+cancelCasual() (client-side 10s guard + DELETE /queue/... on server) BEFORE nav('/lobby'), plus ws_game finally block pops MATCHED_USERS[u_id_str] as belt-and-suspenders. (2) jump broadcast — Player._jump_start_ms=0 by default; ws 'jump' handler starts 650ms arc; Player.to_state() applies sin-arc-lifted Y for humans (bots update y directly in _tick_bots and are exempt). Client engine.js already emitted onLocalUpdate({type:'jump'}) on Space; Game.jsx now forwards it via sockRef.current?.send({type:'jump'}). Full remote-jump visibility requires two clients — single-client E2E only verifies the WS wire; backend unit test in /app/backend/tests/test_jump_broadcast.py covers the server-side arc computation directly.
rca of the issue: Bounce-back RCA: /lobby QueueContext background poll (~3s) checks MATCHED_USERS server state. When user pressed EXIT, WS closed but server on-disconnect cleanup was delayed 5-10s, during which the poll saw matched:true and nav('/play')ed back. Fix: three layers — (a) handleExit sets client-side cancelGuardUntilRef=+10s so poll is ignored, (b) DELETE /queue/{ranked,casual} clears MATCHED_USERS server-side, (c) ws_game finally pops MATCHED_USERS[u_id_str] as fallback for crashes/tab-closes. Jump-broadcast RCA: to_state() previously always used self.y for humans, and there was no field to represent a client-initiated jump — remote clients only saw pitch/yaw. Fix: added _jump_start_ms to Player, WS 'jump' handler starts arc, to_state() computes elevated Y via 650ms sin arc for humans mid-jump; client-side interp (added iter_23) smooths the raise/lower on remote meshes.
